svg.aria-label: As-built CN2 interception: the controller board and front panel wired through all four channels of a real BSS138 level-shifter module, photographed and rotated so its HV pads face the machine, to a XIAO ESP32-C3.
svg.text: CN2 interception — AS BUILT, straight-through, and grouped by device

Converter channel N carries pin DN, and the HV side groups by device: ch1/ch2 are the controller, ch3/ch4 the panel. Every signal crosses a BSS138 channel. Only CN2 pins 1 and 2 are cut — pins 3 and 4 stay connected controller↔panel, because the panel is powered through them.
Blue = toward the ESP32 (an OEM output drives it). Green = out of the ESP32 (it drives an OEM input). Every wire keeps exactly one driver.

g.text: own MCU · owns the whole UI

g.text: ch1 CONTROLLER pin 1 TX out → HV1 · LV1 → D1 / GPIO3 Serial0 RX
ch2 CONTROLLER pin 2 RX in ← HV2 · LV2 ← D2 / GPIO4 Serial0 TX
ch3 PANEL pin 1 RX in ← HV3 · LV3 ← D3 / GPIO5 Serial1 TX
ch4 PANEL pin 2 TX out → HV4 · LV4 → D4 / GPIO6 Serial1 RX

svg.text: The two receive paths prove themselves — every frame carries an XOR. The two transmit paths are blind, and are proven only by the far end’s watchdog staying quiet: the controller reports E5 in status byte 3 bit 6, the panel only on its display.
The pin map is not hard-coded. POST /api/detect counts edges to find the two driven pins, then reads one frame off each — header 0xA2 is the controller, 0xAA is the panel. It never drives a line.
